items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the public health law, in relation to enacting the "fair access to individualized residences (FAIR) act"
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S6767

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the public health law, in relation to enacting the
"fair access to individualized residences (FAIR) act"

 PURPOSE :

To direct the state to develop and implement a clear, consistent and
uniform policy for ensuring that priority for residential placements
of individuals with developmental disabilities includes individuals
who can no longer be cared for safely by their families

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1 of the bill provides a legislative intent.

Section 2 establishes that the law shall be known as the FAIR ACT
(Fair Access to Individualized Residences).

Section 3 adds a new section 207-a to the public health law
establishing a priority placement process for certain developmental
disabled persons.

Sections 4 and 5 require the Commissioners of Health and Developmental
Disabilities to implement the provisions of the act within 120 of the
effective date which shall be immediately.

 JUSTIFICATION :

In the face of insufficient resources for residential development the
waitlist for people with developmental disabilities in need of out of
home residential placement has grown to crisis proportions. Further
budget resources are heavily focused on the placement of people
considered "special populations," rather than people who have lived at
home with family their entire life.

In fact, approximately 25% of the people with developmental
disabilities that reside with family caregivers are living with
caregivers over the age of 60. (SOURCE: Braddock, Hemp, Rizzolo,
Tanis, Haffer, & Wu. (2015). State of the States in Developmental
Disabilities: Emerging from the Great Recession. Boulder/Chicago:
Universities of Colorado & Illinois). This translates to approximately
50,000 New Yorkers. Due to the increasing age related disabilities of
their family caregivers, particularly elderly parents, many are living
under circumstances often significantly more difficult than persons
designated as special population. Their family caregivers have
provided extensive supports which have reduced the need for government
expenditures over many years. That contribution must be recognized as
part of a process that allocates placements based on individual need
rather than an individual's designation as the member of a particular
class of people.

In view of the urgency of the waiting list crisis and resource
limitations, it is imperative that the State develop a clear, open and
transparent policy for ensuring that placements go to those
individuals who are most in need. This must take into account the
circumstances of family caregivers including age, disability and the
means to continue to support their loved on at home.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

New Bill

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :
None to state.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
Immediately and the Commissioners shall implement the provisions of
the act within 120 of the effective date.

A.actClause: AN ACT to amend the mental hygiene law, in relation to enacting the "fair access to individualized residences (FAIR) act"
A.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S6767A

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the mental hygiene law, in relation
to enacting the "fair access to individualized residences (FAIR) act"

 PURPOSE :

To direct the state to develop and implement a caregiver assessment
for ensuring that priority for residential placements of individuals
with developmental disabilities includes individuals who can no longer
be cared for safely by their families

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1 of the bill provides a legislative intent.

Section 2 establishes that the law shall be known as the FAIR ACT
(Fair Access to Individualized Residences).

Section 3 adds a new section 41.59 to the mental hygiene law
establishing a caregiver assessment for ensuring priority placement
process for certain developmental disabled persons.

Sections 4 the effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

In the face of insufficient resources for residential development the
waitlist for people with developmental disabilities in need of out of
home residential placement has grown to crisis proportions. Further
budget resources are heavily focused on the placement of people
considered "special populations," rather than people who have lived at
home with family their entire life.

In fact, approximately 25% of the people with developmental
disabilities that reside with family caregivers are living with
caregivers over the age of 60. (SOURCE: Braddock, Hemp, Rizzolo,
Tanis, Haffer, & Wu. (2015). State of the States in Developmental
Disabilities: Emerging from the Great Recession. Boulder/Chicago:
Universities of Colorado & Illinois). This translates to approximately
50,000 New Yorkers. Due to the increasing age related disabilities of
their family caregivers, particularly elderly parents, many are living
under circumstances often significantly more difficult than persons
designated as special population. Their family caregivers have
provided extensive supports which have reduced the need for government
expenditures over many years. That contribution must be recognized as
part of a process that allocates placements based on individual need
rather than an individual's designation as the member of a particular
class of people.

In view of the urgency of the waiting list crisis and resource
limitations, it is imperative that the State develop a caregiver
assessment process for ensuring that placements go to those
individuals who are most in need. This must take into account the
circumstances of family caregivers including age, disability and the
means to continue to support their loved on at home.

This bill directs the commissioner to develop an assessment process in
consultation with the developmental disabilities advisory council and
other interested parties and provides time from for the assessments to
be performed upon request of a caregiver or individual, including time
frames for decisions and appeals of those decisions.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

New Bill
 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None to state.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
Immediately and the Commissioners shall adopt any rules or regulations
necessary to implement the provisions of this act to take effect by
March 1, 2017.

summary: Enacts the "fair access to individualized residences (FAIR) act" to provide for family caregiver assessments for developmentally disabled persons living at home, who are on the residential request list maintained by the office for people with developmental disabilities.
